MonitoringProgramDescription:
Quagga and zebra mussels need calcium to build their shells, so the calcium in the water is one measure of where they could take hold if they arrived. TRPA samples calcium at 77 marinas, boat ramps, creek mouths, and other nearshore sites.

Environmental DNA (eDNA) sampling filters water for the genetic traces that plants and animals leave behind, which can show that an invasive species is present before anyone sees it. In July and August 2024, five agencies collected 103 eDNA samples, nearly all at creek mouths.
MonitoringApproach:
Each calcium sample records the site, date, depth, calcium reading, conductivity, and water temperature. Readings were taken in 2021 and 2025. Twelve records dated 2026 have no readings yet. Each site is assigned a sample year from 2025 to 2027, so about a third of the sites are sampled each year.

Each eDNA sample records the sampling agency, site, bottom sediment, and number of filters used. TRPA collected 69 of the 103 samples. The Lahontan Water Board, the Nevada Division of Environmental Protection, the UC Davis Tahoe Environmental Research Center, and the California Tahoe Conservancy collected the rest. The map service holds no lab results for them yet.

Read the first survey with care. The April 2021 readings, with a median of 37, run three to four times higher than the July 2021 and June 2025 readings, with medians of 11 and 10. The map service does not say why, so the first survey may not be comparable with the later ones, and the ranking here uses 2025 only.

The map service labels calcium readings in parts per billion. Confirm the unit before comparing a reading with a published mussel threshold. Thirteen calcium samples have no site name, and 54 have no conductivity reading.
